# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 42 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 42 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_042_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 11, Part 1 — Discerning the True and False Prophet

**42:1** He showed me men seated on a bench and another man seated in a chair. And he said to me: "Do you see the men seated on the bench?" "I see them, lord," I replied. "These," he said, "are the faithful; and he who sits in the chair is a false prophet who is corrupting the understanding of the servants of God — that is, of the double-minded, not the faithful."

**42:2** "These double-minded persons come to him as to a soothsayer and consult him about what will happen to them. And that false prophet, having no power of the divine Spirit within himself, speaks with them in accordance with their inquiries and the desires of their wicked hearts, and he fills their souls as they desire. For being empty himself, he gives empty answers to those who are empty. For whatever word is asked of him, he speaks — he speaks from the emptiness of his own heart. Yet at times he happens to speak some word correctly, because the devil fills him with the intention that some of his words may come true, in order that this prophet may have greater confidence and that the double-minded may come to him in greater numbers, so that he may lead them more effectively astray."

**42:3** "All those, therefore, who are strong in the faith of the Lord do not consult him, knowing that there is no truth in him. For no spirit given by God requires to be questioned; but since it possesses the power of the divine, it speaks of itself, because it speaks as God wills. Therefore when the man who possesses the divine Spirit enters into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and the assembly of those men offers prayer, then the angel of the prophetic Spirit, who rests upon him, fills that man, and the man, being filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the congregation as the Lord wills."

**42:4** "In this way the divine Spirit will be made manifest. Whatever power, therefore, the divine Spirit possesses to speak — that power is of the Lord. Hear therefore concerning the Spirit that is from God and concerning the false spirit, so that you may believe the true Spirit and not put your trust in the false one."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and pneumatological precision.*
